name: Guardian cryptic crossword, Penguin book 11 No 28
preamble: Solve the clues and fit the solutions into the diagram jigsaw-wise, wherever they will go.

clue.text: F — for Fraser — was her brother's wife
Lout made out to be deprived of life
Out of court is fruit, as lemon's classed
See H Put in chair, wild hornet goes in last
Flu developed through this Roman lass
Nerve attached to quantity of gas
or Stone the stubborn brute for little growth
Seat for squat round model egg that quoth …
Rough in temper, skill to which cloud thickens'
Either litigant or sleigh-bells (Dickens)
King first with king's evil's silver grip
Place one can get quiet and have a kip
Anthem word's translated, and is too
Nature's other choice, to form run true
Person looked at with unfocused view
Broken off by tripper, were IU
This will make one score a century
Group of atoms: tinkering's not for me
Boy that's eating grass? Exactly so
Less chaotic princess in a row
Raised time off: force open or collapse
Girl I went with proved OK, perhaps
Anti-friction plate gives owner air
New dry axe is photographed with care
Soft and weak in leg — do it yourself
Final group's (say) wise with Polish pelf
